title: Eva Zemberi Applies 'Unusual Failure' to Digital Health: 'Their Own Success Destroys Them'
summary: Digital health operator Eva Zemberi takes Eric's 'unusual failure' concept from Incorruptible and shows how it plays out in healthcare product scaling — a pattern Eric reposted as 'the concept in the wild.'
blockquote:
Some companies don't fail because they're wrong.

They fail because their own success destroys them.

I heard Eric Ries describe this as "unusual failure" in a recent conversation about his upcoming book "Incorruptible".

In digital health, I see a version of this over and over:
Early success gives teams permission—and pressure—to make the wrong decisions.

source_urls.label: Eric's repost: 'the concept in the wild'
